sourceName: ARC Centre of Excellence for Automated Decision-Making and Society
title: ADM+S recommendations cited in Senate Digital Duty of Care report
headline: Senate inquiry report cites ADM+S recommendations on Digital Duty of Care
summary: The Senate inquiry into the Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill 2026 has released its report following public hearings and submissions. The report acknowledges recommendations from the ADM+S Centre regarding an outcomes-based duty of care for online services. These recommendations include extending protections against serious online harms to adults and enabling independent research into platforms.
why_it_matters: The proposed legislation signals a shift toward outcomes-based regulation for digital services, which may require Australian organisations to adopt broader risk management frameworks to address systemic harms beyond specific, narrow risks.

quotes.text: The committee’s report acknowledged ADM+S support for an outcomes-based duty requiring online services to take appropriate action to ensure a safe online environment.
the Centre argued this approach would be better equipped to address broader, systemic and emerging online harms than previous regulatory approaches focused on narrow, specific risks.

dates_mentioned.quote: Released on Friday 20 November 2026, the report follows an inquiry into the Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill 2026

classification.significance_reason: The report reflects significant legislative progress on a proposed duty of care framework that would impact how digital services manage systemic risks in Australia.
